debate.said: Here is the case for owning Taiwan Semiconductor (ADR). Revenue is growing 50.9% year over year (strong). Earnings changed +68.7% versus a year ago. Operating margin is 58.0%.
I'm not convinced. Price is 15.2% below its 200-day average: the long-term trend is down. Annualised volatility is 46%. Over 6 months it returned -19.3% versus -1.7% for the MSCI World benchmark.
Price action is noise over a few weeks; the business is what we own — revenue is growing 50.9% year over year (strong). Weakness can be an entry point.

risk: Maximum position size: 10% of the portfolio (scaled for 46% volatility).
Every order costs a €1 fee, like on Trade Republic. Stop-loss rule: review at -15% from cost.
chair: Weighted committee score is +0.28 on a scale of -1 to +1; 3 of 5 analysts lean the same way. Conviction: Medium.
Decision: BUY. We propose a position of up to 10% of the portfolio.
